entities.name: Mursili I
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Mursili I was a king of the Hittites (c. 1620–1590 BCE on the middle chronology) who extended Old Kingdom power through dramatic long-range campaigns. Most famously, he raided down the Euphrates and sacked Babylon, ending the First Dynasty of Babylon (Hammurabi's line) and scrambling Mesopotamian politics—an extraordinary projection of Anatolian arms into the alluvial south.

His reign also pressed into Syria, continuing Hittite interest in the Amorite and Hurrian zones that linked Anatolia to Mesopotamia. Yet success abroad did not secure the court: Mursili was assassinated in a palace conspiracy, and the Old Kingdom slid into dynastic turmoil.

He remains the emblem of early Hittite overreach—capable of toppling Babylon, unable to stabilise succession—setting problems that later New Kingdom great kings would inherit.
